title: Signatura Rerum, the Signature of All Things
author: Jakob Bohme
description: Signatura Rerum: The Signature of All Things by Jakob Böhme (1622), in the English translation by John Ellistone (1651), often reprinted in Everyman's Library. In it the Silesian mystic shows how the inner spiritual essence of every created thing is expressed in its outward form, colour, smell and sound, its 'signature', so that nature is a language revealing God. Böhme describes the seven qualities or forms of eternal nature by which the divine will manifests out of the Ungrund, the generation of the 'eternal word', the contest of wrath and love, and the redemption of fallen creation through Christ. He uses the language of alchemy (salt, sulphur and mercury, the philosophers' stone, the planetary metals) as a symbolic key to the soul's rebirth. It is foundational for Christian theosophy, Paracelsian correspondence theory and the doctrine of signatures in esoteric medicine.
